location.basis: Published positions only: Wikipedia gives 23.6304 N, 70.8407 E (23 deg 37 min 49 s N, 70 deg 50 min 27 s E) and OpenStreetMap (Nominatim, archaeological_site) gives 23.62614 N, 70.83986 E. We could not confirm the mound on the imagery, so the position is not verified.

main_system_reason: No system: we could not identify the site on the imagery.
notes: The Esri imagery is a Vantor Vivid mosaic of 26 March 2026 with real detail to zoom 18 (0.55 m per pixel). We searched both published positions and the surrounding 1.8 km. The Wikipedia point falls in cultivated fields beside a seasonal stream, and the OpenStreetMap point, 470 m further south, lies in scrub on the west shore of a small reservoir. Neither area shows a mound with a fortification line, a fenced protected area or any straight wall. The excavations of 1971-72 exposed a small fortified settlement of about 1.4 ha; they appear to have been backfilled and the site is overgrown, or the published positions are off by more than our search radius. Stepped pale terraces about 1.2 km south of the Wikipedia point (23.6194 N, 70.8434 E) are quarry or field terraces, not Harappan architecture. Surkotada is therefore not measurable from this imagery.
